in_hebrew.name: ספפירה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם ספפירה נגזר מיוונית ופירושו כחול או צבע תכלת
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ספפירה מקורו ביוונית ופירושו כחול או צבע תכלת. השם קשור למונח היווני 'σάπφειρος' (sappheiros), שפירושו אבן ספיר או צבע כחול כהה. באתרוגיה הנוצרית, השם ספפירה משויך לאישה שחיה בתקופת האלף הראשון לספירה ונודעה באדיקותה ובאומץ לבה. השם גם מופיע בברית החדשה, בספר מעשי השליחים, שם מוזכרת ספפירה כאשתו של אנניה, שנענשו על שקרם לרוח הקודש.

in_greek.name: Σαφφείρη
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Σαφφείρη σημαίνει μπλε ή κυανό χρώμα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σαφφείρη προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'σάπφειρος' (sappheiros), που σημαίνει μπλε ή κυανό χρώμα. Στην πρωτοχριστιανική εποχή, το όνομα Σαφφείρη συνδέθηκε με την αρετή και την πνευματική αγνότητα. Στο Καινόν Διαθήκη, συγκεκριμένα στους Πράξεις των Αποστόλων, αναφέρεται η Σαφφείρη ως η σύζυγος του Ανανία, που μαζί με τον συζύγο της αντιμετώπισε τις συνέπειες της ψευδούς μαρτυρίας τους ενώπιον του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Sapphirae
in_latin.meaning: The name Sapphirae means blue or azure color

in_english.name: Sapphirae
in_english.meaning: The name Sapphirae signifies blue or azure, symbolizing purity and virtue
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sapphirae derives from the Greek 'σάπφειρος' (sappheiros), signifying the blue or azure color, and by extension, spiritual purity and virtue. Historically, Sapphirae is noted in the New Testament, specifically in Acts 5:1-11, as the wife of Ananias, who, along with her husband, was found guilty of lying to the Holy Spirit. The name has been adopted in Christian traditions to signify faithfulness, honesty, and spiritual integrity. In modern usage, Sapphirae remains a unique and meaningful name among Christian communities worldwide.

biblical_reference.note: Sapphirae, along with her husband Ananias, was a follower of Christ in the early Christian church, known for their deceitful actions against the Holy Spirit.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sapphirae is rooted in ancient Jewish history and connected to the beautiful and precious stone, the sapphire. In Eastern cultures, the sapphire is associated with royalty, wisdom, and strength. It is also said to symbolize trust, clairvoyance, and inner peace. Naming a child Sapphirae could evoke images of beauty, preciousness, and the remarkable qualities associated with the gem.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Sapphirae symbolizes the purity and foundational elements of the faith, as mentioned in the Bible's tabernacle construction. The name evokes spiritual depth, faith, and a connection to the divine. It may also be seen as a reminder of God's presence throughout history and the precious value of His faithful followers. The name inspires a sense of devotion, strength, and the importance of maintaining a pure and unyielding faith in God.

historical_references.reference: In Roman mythology, Sapphira was the goddess of health and fertility. She was often identified with the Greek goddess of the same name, Aphrodite, who was also associated with health and fertility. Sapphira was believed to have the power to heal diseases, particularly those affecting the genitals and the eyes.

In early Christian tradition, Sapphira was one of the seven deacons of the early Christian church, along with Phoebe, Prisca, Euodia, Nympha, and Helena. She and her husband Ananias were celebrated for their charitable works and were said to have sold their property and donated the proceeds to the church. However, they kept back some of the money for themselves and lied about it, leading to their deaths as a result of divine punishment.
